events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.92)
events.body:
This is a route_deviation case on a fixed-fare RydeX booking. The GPS record establishes one off-route segment: 09:06–09:13, 4.84 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.00 km, up to 1176 m off route [F3], with actual distance 21.6 km vs 16.6 km optimal (+5.0 km) [F1]. Under RD-1 that segment is an off-route segment requiring review against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5.

No exemption applies. RD-4(a) requires a traffic incident on the replaced optimal stretch within the matching radius; no incident is recorded near the route during the trip window [F12], and the AYE band 5 (40–49 km/h) and CTE band 4 (30–39 km/h) records [F10][F11] are neither band 1 nor band 2 and, under RD-4(b), cannot exempt a segment on their own. claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver drove 21.6 km against an optimal 16.6 km (+5.0 km, +30%), and 4.84 km of that was a single off-route segment between 09:06 and 09:13 where the optimal route covers 0.00 km (wandering up to 1176 m off the route).

No exemption applies to that segment: the driver's own written statement admits a reroute ('I followed my GPS; it rerouted me') without any rider consent, and the chat contains no rider agreement to a route change before the segment began — only pickup messages at 08:49.

The reroute was not justified: traffic records show only AYE speed band 5 (40-49 km/h) and CTE band 4 (30-39 km/h), i.e. free-flowing moderate traffic, and no traffic incidents at all near the route during the trip window, so RD-4's reasonable-cause exemption cannot apply to the 4.84 km segment.

This trip is a RydeX fixed-fare booking (service is non-metered: the estimate was 16.6 km / 22 min and the rider was charged a flat $34.38 with no surge), so the 4.84 km of extra driving generated no recoverable fare, and the complaint about 'extra distance' must be resolved as a fee/item review rather than a mileage refund.

The fare breakdown contains no unapproved add-on to refund: billed distance 16.6 km does not exceed the optimal route, surge is 1.0x, and waiting fee is $0.00, so base + distance + time + platform fee ($3.90 + $23.39 + $5.62 + $1.47 = $34.38) is the only money charged, and under RD-2 the recoverable amount here is 0.

Although no money is refundable on this non-metered fare, the driver's unannounced 4.84 km deviation still breaches the duty to take the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, so a violation of RD-1 should be recorded against this trip.

The driver's account shows 2 disputes in the last 90 days but 0 upheld and no prior route finding, so the RD-6 'repeated' threshold (at least one established route dispute in 90 days) is not met and no flag_account is requested for this driver.

weaknesses: The strongest point against the refund request is the fare itself: F4 and F6 show the rider was billed for 16.6 km against a 16.6 km optimal route on a fixed RydeX price, so the extra 4.84 km (F3) produced no extra charge and RD-2 yields a recoverable amount of $0.

The driver will argue a justified reroute, and F9 records his claim that his GPS rerouted him; RD-4 is the clause the other side will lean on, though F10/F11 (bands 5 and 4, i.e. not severe congestion) and F12 (no incidents) do not support an exemption.

The rider's own complaint says 'the app estimated 17 km ... the meter came to 17 km', which is inconsistent with the GPS record of 21.6 km actual (F1) and with the billed 16.6 km (F4); the rider's statement is also weakened by F7/F8 showing no in-app route objection was ever raised.

claims.assertion: This trip was a RydeX fixed-fare booking, so the fare did not vary with distance: the rider was billed on a 16.6 km distance basis, exactly the optimal route length, with no excess distance billed.

Because the billed distance (16.6 km) equals the optimal distance (16.6 km), the GPS-observed off-route segment added no chargeable distance to this fare, so the amount that can be refunded under RD-2 for a non-metered service is SGD 0.00.
No unpublished or unsupported add-on was charged: waiting fee is $0.00, surge multiplier is 1.0x, and the only add-on is the published $1.47 platform fee, so FARE-1 discloses no item to refund.

weaknesses: The GPS record does show a real deviation: F3 documents an off-route segment 09:06-09:13 covering 4.84 km where the optimal route covers 0.00 km, and F1 shows actual 21.6 km vs optimal 16.6 km (+5.0 km, +30%) with F2 showing 32.7 min vs 22 min estimated. The other side will argue under RD-1 that any unexplained deviation breaches the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty, and there is no rider consent in the chat (F7, F8) before the deviation.

My congestion argument under RD-4 is weak on its own terms: F10 and F11 are traffic-band facts, and RD-4(b) says bands alone do not justify a reroute in the MVP; RD-4(a) requires an incident within 300 m of the optimal route, and F12 records no incidents at all.
